full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-8 to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 9-7-2019 passed by the learned Judge (Joint District and Sessions Judge) of Land Survey Tribunal, Khulna in Suit No. Land 580 of 2014 rejecting an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 read with section 145A/145D of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for rejection of plaint should not be set-aside and/or such other or further or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts in short are that the opposite party Nos. 1-8 as plaintiffs filed Land Tribunal Suit No.580 of 2014 under section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for correction of record-of-right against the petitioners and opposite party Nos.9-11 who were defendants. 

 3. In above suit defendants filed a petition under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure, 1908 for rejection of plaint. It was alleged that before the establishment of Land Survey Tribunal plaintiff filed Title Suit No.1105 of 2008 for the self same property praying and for same relief in which defendants are party and above suit is pending for trial in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna. In violation of Section 145(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 plaintiffs have filed this second suit for the same property so the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 6. Mr Md Mamun Aleem, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the opposite parties filed a suit for correction of record-of-rights before establishment of the Land Survey Tribunal that suit could be brought to the tribunal under section 145A(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. A new and second suit for the same cause was barred by law. 

 7. The learned Advocate further submits that since the Judge of the tribunal is appointed from among the Joint District Judge of the judicial service and the words “suit” “judgment” and “decree” have been used in section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the tribunal may be declared as a civil court and judgment, decree and order of the tribunal may be made subject to appeallate and revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division. In support of above submissions the learned Advocate refers to the case laws reported in 17 BLC (AD) 50, 51 DLR (AD) 228, 10 DLR 527 and 68 DLR 463. 

 10. At the outset it is to be mentioned that Chapter XVIIA of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was introduced in the above Act by Act No. IX of 2004 for establishment of land Survey Tribunal for entertaining only the suits arising out of final publication of the last revised record-of-rights. In 2004 the last revised record-of-right was the Bangladesh survey or BS khatian. The land survey tribunal has been vested with jurisdiction to determine the correction or falsity of BS khatians. The tribunal has no jurisdiction to determine or declare right to property or right to office which a Civil Court has.
